summary.title: Behavior-driven development - Wikipedia
summary.one_liner: BDD is an agile practice where business and technical people agree on desired behavior, write it as structured natural-language scenarios (Given/When/Then), and turn those into executable tests.
keywords: what is bdd in plain english
takeaways: BDD aims for a shared understanding of the problem among business, developers and QA, not just a refinement of TDD.
Behaviour is specified as user stories with a narrative (As a / I want / so that) and acceptance scenarios (Given / When / Then).
BDD tools parse the ubiquitous language in specifications and turn each clause into parameters for executable tests.
Specification tools use technical, function-level specs as a lower-level complement to story-based testing.
The three amigos meeting (business, development, testing) is used to uncover missing specifications before building.
summary.summary: This Wikipedia article defines behavior-driven development as an agile method centred on collaboration between business and IT people to reach a shared understanding of a problem. It explains the principles of naming tests by desired behaviour, the user story format with Given/When/Then scenarios (Gherkin in Cucumber), and the use of a ubiquitous language from domain-driven design. It also covers BDD tooling, the difference between story-based and specification-based tools, and the "three amigos" workshop. The page is mostly conceptual and includes a short stack example and a reference list.
